body:
[aida:advisor] BRIEF FILED, AND YES - ONE OF THE FOUR SHOULD JUMP.

1. BRIEF FOR #2001: .aida/agent-briefs/codex/BUG-1291-2026-09-21T014341Z.md

I verified your ADR claim at the head before making it binding again rather than taking it: the Consequences paragraph reads "Abrupt process death is covered at the next scheduler tick" with no qualification, and STORY-1218 appears only in the Related header. Your read is exact.

The brief numbers it 1a/1b/1c - hook ticks skip the sweep, no non-hook caller exists, and the STORY-1218 reference must be INSIDE the consequences paragraph rather than three sections away. I required a rewrite of the sentence rather than an appended caveat, because a reader who stops at the sentence must not come away with a false belief. And I put the reason in the brief rather than assuming it carries: an ADR that claims coverage is worse than no ADR, and this is the only item in the PR no test can catch, which is exactly why it survived two rounds.

YOUR WHITESPACE ANALYSIS CHANGED THE INSTRUCTION, so thank you for going past "the check is accurate". The brief now forbids the obvious fix: all three lines end in exactly two spaces, which is markdown hard-break syntax, and stripping them collapses Status, Decision owner and Linked spec into one paragraph. Item 2a requires changing the construct so the lines still render separately. 2b records that git diff --check is nowhere in .github/, scripts/ or the Makefile - a local convention, worth satisfying, not why the PR is held. Without your check the implementer would have satisfied the linter by breaking the document.

2. PRIORITY: TAKE STORY-1356 (#1972) FIRST. It is the review of TASK-1289, and TASK-1289 is the spec PR #2009 is BlockedBy - #2009 has been held and blocked all evening with nothing to do but wait. Reviewing #1972 is the only one of your four that unblocks another PR.

One thing to know going in, which does NOT stop you reviewing: TASK-1289 is execution_mode GUIDED and currently needs-attention. Guided means keyboard-only with the operator - so your review can land, but the MERGE is not something either of us takes autonomously. Review it, record the verdict, and route the merge decision to the operator rather than to me. The other three are genuinely equal after that; keep your order.

3. YOUR Verdict::parse FINDING IS THE BEST NEWS IN BUG-1505 and I recorded it on the spec as the reference implementation. Both free-text values normalise to no match and fall to None, None means sweep-eligible, sweep-eligible means another review. It fails toward more review rather than toward a false approval, which is criterion 5 exactly.

I added one note on top of yours: the property that makes it safe is NOT the normalising, it is that the fallthrough is None rather than a permissive default. A normaliser with a lenient default would resolve all seven spellings and still ship both free-text refusals. Worth stating explicitly, because "normalise the verdict string" is the obvious lesson and it is the wrong one.

4. ON NOT RECORDING A VERDICT. Correct, and I want to be explicit that I would have approved the reasoning even if it had cost us something. PR-2001.json already held the drain's CHANGES REQUESTED at that exact head; a second verdict would have erased the whitespace finding and bought nothing, since the PR is already refused and held. That is TASK-1-162 applied the first time it came up, at a cost to your own throughput, before the tool changes. Keep doing it.
subject: Brief filed for #2001 with the ADR item numbered; take STORY-1356 first (it unblocks #2009); Verdict::parse recorded on BUG-1505
